next_event.source: The 2024 three-year framework ends with FY2026; CFO declined to give a new one at Bernstein SDC 2026-05-28 (document_id 54873). Lexical 'investor day' search over FY2026 calls returned nothing scheduled. Next routine event is Q3 2026 earnings, date not in corpus.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Uber frames profitability as adjusted EBITDA CAGR (high 30s to 40%, 2024 to 2026, from the 2024-02-14 Investor Update) and reports adjusted EBITDA as a percent of gross bookings (4.6% in Q4 2025). No margin level target is public; the score uses a dated EBITDA growth rate, not a margin. Street margins here are EBITDA over revenue (Visible Alpha does not carry gross bookings in this dataset). Uber is not founder-run: Khosrowshahi has been CEO since September 2017 (DEF 14A, document_id 6799); data_comps founder_led is false.

statements.quote: Over the next 3 years, we expect to deliver gross bookings CAGR of mid- to high-teens and adjusted EBITDA CAGR from the high 30s to 40%, with 90% or more annual free cash flow conversion.
statements.speaker: Dara Khosrowshahi

statements.quote: Two years ago, we gave you a 3-year outlook, and I'm pleased to report that we're currently exceeding every target that we set for gross bookings, adjusted EBITDA growth, and free cash flow conversion.
statements.speaker: Dara Khosrowshahi

statements.quote: Our profits compounded at about 50% CAGR in that period of time, relative to the high 30s to 40% CAGR we were talking about.
statements.speaker: Balaji Krishnamurthy

statements.quote: With that sort of a lens, I would think about the path forward as a continued refinement of what we're doing versus something that we need to change, right?
statements.speaker: Balaji Krishnamurthy

street.gap_assumption: Calendar fiscal year, Baba labels match. Framework top (40% CAGR on FY2023 adjusted EBITDA of $4,052M) implies $11,119M for 2026; low end (37%) implies $10,419M. Consensus FY2026 EBITDA is $11,358M, 2.2% above the top of the range. Expressed over consensus FY2026 revenue ($57,899M) the framework top is 19.20% vs consensus 19.62%, so the target sits 41 bps BELOW the street.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha), summary and fundamentals

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 2026, Q2 2026], adjusted EBITDA over revenue from Baba actuals: Q1 18.79% vs 16.20%; Q2 19.86% vs 16.75%. Delivery bookings include Trendyol Go (closed June 2025) and Getir and Careem additions per the Q2 2026 call review (document_id 129329); no Item 2.01 or 1.01 8-K in the window.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: FY2026 consensus EBITDA ($11.36B) is 2.2% above the top of the 2024 framework, and management says it is exceeding every target. The framework was set 2024-02-14 (outside the 18-month window) and the only leadership changes are internal promotions under a CEO in the seat since 2017.
verdict: Not a GXO setup: cheap on its own history after a 32% drawdown, but the CEO has run it since 2017, the new CFO is an internal promotion promising continuity, and the street already models more than the 2024 framework.
open_questions: Will Uber issue a new multi-year framework when the 2024 to 2026 one expires, and would it include a margin-on-gross-bookings target?
Is the multiple compression driven by autonomous-vehicle disruption risk, which no margin framework addresses?
How much of the roughly $10B multi-year AV investment flows through adjusted EBITDA versus investing cash flow?
